items.claim: The mishle-title seam at Prov.1.1 (matching only Prov.10.1, 2 of 915 verses) and the skeleton pair shared between Prov.1.2 and the Prov.1.7 motto re-derive exactly as the row states, and the infinitive-construct chain (Prov.1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, interrupted once at 1.5) matches the pointed text token-for-token.
items.evidence: Byte-tier re-check of oshb Prov.1.1-1.7 confirms: 1.2 opens the infinitive לָדַ֣עַת, 1.3 opens לָ֭קַחַת, 1.4 opens לָתֵ֣ת, 1.6 opens לְהָבִ֣ין -- all infinitive-construct openers -- while 1.5 opens with the finite verb יִשְׁמַ֣ע (the disclosed hearer-clause break); prov_device_inventory.json mishle_verse_initial confirms the 2-of-915 digit. Petuchah at 1.7 passes check_marks.py GREEN (single-witness, correctly disclosed).

items.claim: The vocative-plus-imperative opening at Prov.1.8 and the fresh, distinct vocative-plus-conditional at Prov.1.10 are both real tier-1 seams bounding this two-verse exordium; the short span is self-disclosed and the rejected rival (folding forward into 1.10-1.19) is the genuinely strongest alternative, not a strawman.
items.evidence: Byte-tier check confirms Prov.1.8 opens שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי and Prov.1.10 opens בְּנִ֡י אִם, a distinct construction; adjacent-verse skeleton comparison finds zero shared non-stopword content tokens across the Prov.1.7|1.8 and Prov.1.9|1.10 seams, so no undisclosed cross-seam cohesion contests either boundary.

items.claim: The conditional-plus-quotation structure (Prov.1.10 protasis, 1.11 speech-frame protasis introducing a first-person-plural quotation running through 1.14) and the register shift back to second-person address at the fresh vocative of Prov.1.15 re-derive exactly as stated.
items.evidence: Byte-tier text confirms 1.10 opens בְּנִ֡י אִם יְפַתּ֥וּךָ, 1.11 opens אִם יֹאמְרוּ֮ introducing direct quotation, and 1.15 resumes בְּנִ֗י אַל in the father's second-person voice; check_web_quotes.py GREEN over the row's WEB quotation of 1.14.

items.claim: The fresh vocative-plus-prohibition at Prov.1.15 opening the application, and the closing gnomic summary at Prov.1.19 carrying the petuchah, both re-derive exactly as stated.
items.evidence: Byte-tier text confirms 1.15 opens בְּנִ֗י אַל; petuchah at 1.19 passes check_marks.py GREEN (single-witness, correctly disclosed); adjacent-verse skeleton check across the Prov.1.14|1.15 and Prov.1.19|1.20 seams finds zero undisclosed shared content tokens.

items.claim: The third-person-to-first-person shift at Prov.1.20-1.22 and the petuchah-bounded frame (Prov.1.19 preceding, Prov.1.33 closing) re-derive exactly as stated, and the ketiv/qere note at Prov.1.27 is correctly disclosed as single-witness.
items.evidence: Byte-tier text confirms the 1.20-1.21 third-person narration gives way to first-person reproach opening at 1.22; both petuchah marks (1.19, 1.33) and the 1.27 ketiv/qere note pass check_marks.py GREEN. Adjacent-verse skeleton check across the Prov.1.33|2.1 seam finds zero shared content tokens, so no undisclosed cross-seam cohesion contests the closing boundary.

items.claim: The row's claim of a "fourfold protasis running through Prov.2.4" overstates the count: WEB itself glosses Prov.2.2 as a purpose clause, “so as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;” (web:Prov.2.2), not a fourth conditional, so the byte-grounded structure is three protases (2.1, 2.3, 2.4, each opening on a conditional particle) plus one dependent infinitive clause (2.2), not four parallel "if" clauses.
items.evidence: verse_map_web.json Prov.2.2 renders “so as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;” (web:Prov.2.2) -- no "if"; oshb Prov.2.2 opens with the bare infinitive לְהַקְשִׁ֣יב, not a conditional particle, while 2.1/2.3/2.4 each open on a conditional particle. The row's overall boundary (Prov.2.1-2.22 as one instruction_lecture, on the single vocative firing once and the chapter's one-long-sentence grammar) is unaffected by this internal miscount; only the internal-texture description needs the digit corrected from four protases to three protases plus one purpose clause.

items.claim: Three compounding, byte-verifiable defects in this row's seam evidence: (1) "bni_address inventory: 17 tokens book-wide" cites the superseded pre-E-1 figure -- the orchestrator-corrected count (prov_device_inventory.json, TOOLKIT.md) is 22 vocative verses, exactly the stale-figure defect class the campaign flagged; (2) the row's own boundary-driving claim that "the couplets beginning at 3.5 each name אֶל directly" is byte-false (see P02-002 for the full sweep); (3) Prov.4.10 is wrongly counted among "the four verse-initial address slots" -- its first word is the imperative שְׁמַ֣ע, with בְּ֭נִי only the SECOND token, the same construction as Prov.1.8, not a verse-initial vocative like 3.1, 3.21, and 4.20.
items.evidence: sweep.py --heb against verse_map_oshb.json: the exact pointed token אֶל occurs at only 17 verses book-wide (byte tier), none of them Prov.3.7/3.9/3.11/3.12; prov_device_inventory.json bni_address.count = 22 (E-1 corrected), not 17; direct byte read of oshb Prov.4.10 shows the verse opens שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי (imperative first, vocative second) versus oshb Prov.3.1/3.21/4.20 which each open with the vocative as the first word. The row's actual boundary (3.1-3.4 ending before the petuchah at 3.4, distinguishing it from the divine-name-bearing couplets that follow) is not disturbed by any of the three defects -- the divine name is genuinely absent from 3.1-3.4 and present from 3.5 onward (accent_stripped tier) -- but every citation offered in support of that boundary in this row is either stale or wrong.

items.claim: "five אֶל tokens across the row's eight verses" at 3.5/3.7/3.9/3.11/3.12 is byte-false and conflates three distinct Hebrew words: only Prov.3.5 carries the pointed preposition אֶל (twice, within that one verse); Prov.3.7, 3.9, and 3.12 instead carry אֶת (the object marker, different consonants), and Prov.3.11 carries אַל (the negative particle "do not", a true skeleton-homograph of אֶל but differently pointed). The word that genuinely recurs at exactly those five verses is the divine name יְ֭הוָה.
items.evidence: sweep.py --heb on the exact pointed token אֶל (byte tier) returns 17 book-wide hits, with Prov.3.5 the only hit in this row's Prov.3.5-3.12 span; direct byte read of the four other cited verses shows the object-marker form at Prov.3.7/3.9/3.12 and the negative particle at Prov.3.11, never the preposition. sweep.py --heb on the divine name (accent_stripped tier, citation-grade per collate.py convention) returns exactly Prov.3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.11, 3.12 within this row's span (plus 3.26/3.32/3.33 beyond it) -- the row's central "naming density" claim and its rejected_alternative (that the internal petuchah at 3.10 falls inside one continuous naming unit rather than at an edge) both rest on the fabricated citation. Substituting the correct object (the divine name) would still support the same non-split conclusion, but the row as drafted cites the wrong Hebrew word five times as its load-bearing tier-1 evidence.
